`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

209	### 4.2 VideoHungarianMatcher：一次 LSAP 匹配整条时空管道
210	
211	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
212	
213	`VideoHungarianMatcher` 与图像版 `HungarianMatcher` 逐行对比后会发现：**代价函数、随机采样、fp32 防抖、LSAP 求解全部相同**，唯一的实质差异是 mask 代价的计算维度——图像版把 mask 升成 (Q, 1, H, W) 后采样得到 (Q, K)；视频版把 4D 的 (Q, T, H, W) **直接**交给 `point_sample`，T 被当作「通道维」，采样输出 flatten 后是 (Q, K·T)。
214	
215	为什么必须**按视频整体**做一次匹配，而不是逐帧独立匹配？因为 query 跨帧共享（u9-l2）：一个 query 对一条 tube 的全部 T 帧负责。若逐帧匹配，同一 GT 实例可能在第 1 帧分给 query A、第 2 帧分给 query B，监督信号自相矛盾，模型永远学不出稳定的「一个 query 一条管道」。把整条 tube 的 T 帧代价压缩进代价矩阵的一个元素，LSAP 一旦把 query A 与 GT 管道 g 绑定，A 就要在**所有帧**上同时逼近 g——跨帧身份一致性由此从监督机制层面得到保障。
216	
217	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
218	
219	对 batch 中每个视频 b：
220	
221	```
222	1. 分类代价：out_prob = pred_logits[b].softmax(-1)          → (Q, K+1)
223	   cost_class = -out_prob[:, tgt_ids]                        → (Q, M)
224	2. mask 代价：
225	   out_mask = pred_masks[b]            # (Q, T, H/4, W/4)  不加通道维！
226	   tgt_mask = targets[b]["masks"]      # (M, T, H_pad, W_pad) 已 pad
227	   point_coords = torch.rand(1, K, 2)  # 一组共享的随机归一化坐标
228	   tgt = point_sample(tgt_mask, coords.repeat(M,1,1)).flatten(1)  # (M, K·T)
229	   out = point_sample(out_mask, coords.repeat(Q,1,1)).flatten(1)  # (Q, K·T)
230	   关 autocast 转 fp32：
231	   cost_mask = batch_sigmoid_ce_loss(out, tgt)   # (Q, M)
232	   cost_dice = batch_dice_loss(out, tgt)         # (Q, M)
233	3. C = 2.0·cost_class + 5.0·cost_mask + 5.0·cost_dice   # (Q, M)
234	4. linear_sum_assignment(C.cpu()) → 一对一匹配对
235	```
236	
237	`batch_sigmoid_ce_loss` 中的归一化因子 `hw = inputs.shape[1]` 在视频下变成 \(K \cdot T\)——即每个代价元素是「整条 tube 的所有帧 × 所有点」的平均 BCE，一条 query 与一条 GT 的相似度由全部 T 帧联合决定：
238	
239	\[
240	C_{\text{mask}}(q, m) = \frac{1}{K T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathrm{BCE}\big(p_q(x_k, t),\, g_m(x_k, t)\big)
241	\]
242	
243	两个值得注意的细节：
244	
245	- **matcher 用纯随机采样，loss 用不确定性引导采样**。matcher 的 `torch.rand`（L120）与图像版一致；`get_uncertain_point_coords_with_randomness` 只出现在 criterion 侧。匹配发生在梯度更新之前，随机采样足够稳定且更便宜。
246	- **分辨率不一致无碍**。预测是 1/4 分辨率、GT 是网络输入全尺寸，`point_sample` 的坐标是归一化的 \([0,1]\)，各自乘以各自的空间尺寸后插值，天然对齐——这就是源码注释 `# No need to upsample predictions as we are using normalized coordinates :)` 的含义。
247	
248	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
249	
250	**分类代价**。[matcher.py:105-111](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L105-L111)：softmax 后取负的目标类概率近似 NLL，与图像版逐字相同。
251	
252	**4D mask 直接进 point_sample**。[matcher.py:113-120](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L113-L120)：`out_mask` 形状为 `[num_queries, T, H_pred, W_pred]`，GT `.to(out_mask)` 只转 dtype/device；图像版的 `out_mask[:, None]` 两行被**注释保留**（L117-118），采样点是 `torch.rand(1, num_points, 2)`——所有 query 与 GT 共享同一组坐标，保证代价在相同像素位置间比较。
253	
254	**采样与展平**。[matcher.py:122-132](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L122-L132)：`point_sample` 按 (N, P, 2) 坐标对 (N, C, H, W) 输入采样，输出 (N, P, C)。这里输入的「通道维 C」就是 T，输出 (Q, K, T) 经 `flatten(1)` 变 (Q, K·T)。对比图像版 [matcher.py:117-126](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/matcher.py#L117-L126)：图像版先 `out_mask[:, None]` 升成 (Q, 1, H, W)，输出 (Q, K) 后 `squeeze(1)`，最终是 (Q, K) 的二维代价输入。
255	
256	**fp32 防抖与 LSAP**。[matcher.py:134-151](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L134-L151)：`autocast(enabled=False)` 内转 float32 计算 BCE/Dice 代价（半精度下逐点插值误差会造成匹配抖动，u5-l1 讲过同一动机）；三项代价按 2.0/5.0/5.0 加权合成 (Q, M) 矩阵，`linear_sum_assignment` 求解一对一分配。整个函数被 `@torch.no_grad()` 包裹（L95），不建计算图。
257	
258	**谁消费匹配结果**：`VideoSetCriterion.forward` 对主输出与每组 aux 各调一次（criterion.py L218、L237），每次都是「整条 tube」级别的重新匹配。

307	### 4.3 YTVISEvaluator：从 pred_masks 到 YTVIS AP
308	
309	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
310	
311	`YTVISEvaluator` 是从 IFC 项目移植的 `DatasetEvaluator`，底层依赖仓库自带的 `YTVOS` / `YTVOSeval` api（cocotools 的视频版变体）。它解决的问题是：模型输出的是「每视频 top-10 个 (score, label, T 帧 mask)」，评估器要把它转成 YTVIS json、与 GT 做**tube 级**匹配，输出 AP 系列指标。
312	
313	评估与训练监督是两个独立环节，口径有一处重要差别值得点明：训练的匈牙利匹配在「采样点」上比较 mask（省显存），评估的 IoU 在**全部帧的全部像素**上比较（要权威）。
314	
315	YTVIS 格式的预测条目：
316	
317	```json
318	{
319	  "video_id": 1,
320	  "score": 0.92,
321	  "category_id": 3,
322	  "segmentations": [RLE_t0, RLE_t1, null, RLE_t3, ...]   // 每帧一个 RLE，缺失帧为 null
323	}
324	```
325	
326	GT 标注同构（多了 `areas`、`iscrowd` 等字段），一条 GT 标注就是一条贯穿全视频的实例轨道（u9-l3）。
327	
328	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
329	
330	评估器生命周期（`reset → process × N → evaluate`）与三段式计算：
331	
332	```
333	process（每视频一次）
334	  inputs（单视频 dict，含 video_id/length）+ outputs（inference_video 的 dict）
335	    → instances_to_coco_json_video
336	    → [{video_id, score, category_id, segmentations: [T 个 RLE]}, ...]
337	
338	evaluate（数据集跑完一次）
339	  gather 到主进程 → 落盘 instances_predictions.pth
340	  → _eval_predictions
341	      ① category_id 反映射：模型连续 id → 数据集原始 id
342	      ② 落盘 results.json
343	      ③ _evaluate_predictions_on_coco：
344	           删除 bbox 字段（面积按 mask 算）
345	           YTVOS api loadRes（计算 avg_area）
346	           YTVOSeval(gt, dt)：maxDets=[1,10,100]
347	           evaluate() → accumulate() → summarize()
348	      ④ _derive_coco_results：从 stats 取 8 项指标 ×100 + per-category AP
349	```
350	
351	**时空 IoU** 是整个评估的基石，YTVOSeval 对每对（预测 tube, GT tube）计算：
352	
353	\[
354	\text{IoU}_{\text{tube}}(p, g) = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}|p_t \cap g_t|}{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}|p_t \cup g_t|}
355	\]
356	
357	逐帧累加交集与并集的像素数再相除。三种帧状态的处理：
358	
359	| 该帧预测 | 该帧 GT | 交集 | 并集 |
360	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
361	| 有 | 有 | \(|p_t \cap g_t|\) | \(|p_t \cup g_t|\) |
362	| 无（null） | 有 | 0 | \(|g_t|\)（漏检帧全额惩罚） |
363	| 有 | 无（GT 缺失帧） | 0 | \(|p_t|\)（虚检惩罚） |
364	
365	这个定义意味着：预测只要**漏掉一帧**，该帧整个 GT 面积就进入分母——tube IoU 断崖式下跌。这是 VIS 远难于图像实例分割、AP 数值普遍偏低的算法根源，也是「跨帧身份一致性」被直接量化的方式：一个 query 若中途「换目标」，整条 tube 同时变成一条 FP（对真目标）和一条 FN。
366	
367	**面积分桶口径**：APs/APm/APl 按 `avg_area`（tube 的**逐帧平均面积**，而非全帧总面积）划分，阈值 128²/256²。长视频里的小物体不会因为帧数多、总面积大而被错划为 large。
368

456	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
457	
458	**练习 1**：一条预测 tube 漏掉了 3 帧中的 1 帧（该帧 GT 面积为 A，其余帧完美重叠、每帧面积同为 A），它的 tube IoU 是多少？
459	
460	**答案**：交集 \(= 2A\)（重叠的两帧），并集 \(= 2A + A = 3A\)（漏检帧 GT 全额计入并集），IoU \(= 2/3 \approx 0.667\)。即使其余帧完美，也拿不到 0.75 以上的档位——时空 IoU 对漏帧极其敏感。
461	
462	**练习 2**：`inference_video` 硬编码 `topk(10)`，这对评估指标有什么影响？
463	
464	**答案**：每视频最多 10 条预测进入评估，`maxDets=100` 的 AR100 与 AR10 必然相同（stats[8]==stats[7]），评估器因此只展示到 AR10。同时单一视频实例数通常少于 10，topk 一般不构成瓶颈；但若在实例密集的长视频上评估，可考虑调大该值（需改源码，无配置开关）。
465	
466	**练习 3**：为什么 `_evaluate_predictions_on_coco` 要 `c.pop("bbox", None)`？
467	
468	**答案**：cocotools 体系里若结果带 bbox，面积分桶会改用框面积而非 mask 面积，导致 APs/APm/APl 的口径漂移；Mask2Former 的视频预测本来就没有框（mask classification 范式，u7-l2 讲过占位框问题），删掉 bbox 字段强制 api 按 mask 面积（`avg_area`）分桶，保证与 GT 侧同口径。

482	**预期结果**：损失 dict 30 键、`num_masks=2`；评估侧能打印出 IoU 矩阵与（阶跃式的）AP 值。整个流程 CPU 即可运行，但依赖已安装的 detectron2（criterion 侧），全部**待本地验证**；若环境不可用，第 3-4 步可单独运行（只依赖 pycocotools）。

484	## 6. 本讲小结
485	
486	- `VideoSetCriterion.loss_masks` **完整保留**了图像版的逐点采样损失（不确定性引导 + `point_sample`），真实差异只有两处：GT 因 `prepare_targets` 已 pad 而直接 `torch.cat`，以及 `flatten(0, 1)` 把 (N, T, H, W) 的 tube 拆成 (N·T, 1, H, W) 的帧 mask 逐帧监督。

# u9-l4 视频损失与 YTVIS 评估

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲是视频单元（单元九）的收官，把图像版「先匹配、后监督」的训练监督机制（单元五）推广到视频时空管道（tube），并补齐视频侧的评估闭环。读完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 对比 `VideoSetCriterion.loss_masks` 与图像版 `SetCriterion.loss_masks`，说出两处真实差异（GT 打包方式、`flatten(0,1)` 拆帧）以及一处**容易被误传的差异**（逐点采样其实被完整保留了）。
2. 理解 `num_masks` 归一化在视频下的语义：按「管道数」而非「帧数」归一化，一条 tube 的 T 帧损失相加后除以 tube 数。
3. 解释 `VideoHungarianMatcher` 为什么必须**按视频整体做一次 LSAP**，以及 (Q, T, H, W) 的 4D mask 如何被 `point_sample` 直接消费。
4. 读懂 `YTVISEvaluator` 的三段式评估流程，说清时空 IoU 的计算方式（逐帧交/并累加）、`avg_area` 面积分桶口径，以及 AP/AP50/AP75/APs/APm/APl/AR1/AR10 八项指标的含义。
5. 在 `train_net_video.py` 的 `--eval-only` 路径中定位 YTVIS 评估结果的三处日志输出与两处文件落盘位置。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲默认你已读完 u5-l1（匈牙利匹配器）、u5-l2（图像版逐点 mask 损失）与 u9-l2（视频解码器）。下面把几个关键概念串一遍。

**时空管道（tube）**。视频实例分割（VIS）的输出单位不是「一帧里的一个 mask」，而是「贯穿 T 帧的一条实例管道」：形状为 \((T, H, W)\) 的 mask 序列，同一实例在所有帧中共享同一个 query（u9-l2 讲过 query 跨帧共享）。GT 侧的跨帧关联靠 `gt_ids`（u9-l3）。

**「先匹配、后监督」回顾**。mask classification 范式输出固定 Q 个 query，每视频 GT 管道数不定，须先解 LSAP（线性分配问题）做一对一匹配，未匹配 query 视为 no-object。图像版的流程是：匹配（分类 + 采样点 mask/dice 代价）→ 按匹配对监督（交叉熵 + 逐点 BCE/Dice）。视频版把这两步的对象从「2D mask」换成「tube」，框架一行未大改——这正是本讲要展示的「薄层复用」设计。

**逐点采样损失回顾（u5-l2）**。图像版 `loss_masks` 不在全部像素上算 BCE/Dice，而是用 PointRend 式 K + β 重要性采样：对每个预测 mask 取 12544 个归一化坐标点，用 `point_sample`（双线性插值）同时取预测 logit 与 GT 标签，再算逐点损失。归一化坐标的好处：1/4 分辨率预测与全分辨率 GT 可以直接「对采」，无需上采样。

**RLE 编码回顾（u7-l2）**。二值 mask 压缩成行程编码（Run-Length Encoding）的字典 `{"size": [h, w], "counts": bytes}`，pycocotools 的 `mask_util.encode` 生成。YTVIS 格式里一条标注的 `segmentations` 字段是 T 个 RLE 组成的列表，缺失帧为 `null`。

**PR 曲线与 AP 回顾（u7-l2）**。按置信度排序预测，在不同阈值下统计 TP/FP 得到 PR 曲线，101 点插值求平均精度。YTVIS 的 AP 沿用这套流程，唯一改变是「一个预测」的单位从 image mask 变成 tube，IoU 也换成时空版本（见 4.3.2）。

**本讲涉及的关键术语**：

| 术语 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| tube / 时空管道 | 一个实例贯穿 T 帧的 mask 序列，形状 (T, H, W) |
| 时空 IoU | 两条 tube 的逐帧交集像素总数除以逐帧并集像素总数 |
| LSAP | 线性分配问题，由 `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` 求解 |
| `num_masks` | 损失归一化分母；视频下等于批内 GT 管道总数（跨卡平均） |
| `avg_area` | tube 的逐帧平均面积，YTVIS 面积分桶（APs/APm/APl）的口径 |
| YTVOS / YTVOSeval | YTVIS 数据集的评估 api（从 IFC 项目移植的 cocotools 变体） |

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py` | `VideoSetCriterion`：视频版损失，含 `loss_masks` 的拆帧逐点监督 |
| `mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py` | `VideoHungarianMatcher`：按视频整体的 LSAP 匹配 |
| `mask2former/modeling/criterion.py` | 图像版 `SetCriterion`，用于逐行对比 |
| `mask2former/modeling/matcher.py` | 图像版 `HungarianMatcher`，用于逐行对比 |
| `mask2former_video/data_video/ytvis_eval.py` | `YTVISEvaluator`：预测转 YTVIS json、调 api 评估、指标表 |
| `mask2former_video/data_video/datasets/ytvis_api/ytvos.py` | YTVOS api：加载 GT/预测，`loadRes` 计算 `avg_area` |
| `mask2former_video/data_video/datasets/ytvis_api/ytvoseval.py` | YTVOSeval：时空 IoU、PR 累积、12 项 stats |
| `mask2former_video/video_maskformer_model.py` | `VideoMaskFormer`：criterion 的构建、`inference_video` 的输出契约 |
| `train_net_video.py` | 视频 Trainer：`build_evaluator`、`test`、`--eval-only` 主分支 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 VideoSetCriterion.loss_masks：把时空管道拆成帧，逐点监督

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`VideoSetCriterion` 是图像版 `SetCriterion` 的视频推广。它要解决的问题是：监督对象从「每图 N 个 (H, W) 的 2D mask」变成「每视频 N 条 (T, H, W) 的时空管道」后，逐点采样损失机制如何延续。

先给一个重要结论（也纠正一个常见误传）：**当前 HEAD 的视频版 `loss_masks` 完整保留了 `point_sample` 逐点采样**，并没有退回「全 mask 像素损失」。本讲规格中「找出视频版没有 point_sample 的位置」的预设与源码不符（规格也标注了「待确认：以源码为准」）——以源码为准：`mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py` 的 L157-177 与图像版一样调用了 `get_uncertain_point_coords_with_randomness` 与 `point_sample`。真实差异有两处：

1. **拆帧**：把 (N, T, H, W) 的 tube 用 `flatten(0, 1)` 拆成 (N·T, 1, H, W) 的独立帧 mask，逐帧采样点、逐帧算损失。
2. **GT 打包**：图像版要用 `nested_tensor_from_tensor_list` 处理批内不同尺寸的 GT；视频版因为 `prepare_targets` 已把所有 GT mask 统一 pad 到网络输入尺寸（u9-l1 讲过的 `mask_shape` 硬对齐），直接 `torch.cat` 即可。

而归一化语义的变化才是「取舍」所在：分母 `num_masks` 数的是**管道数**，不是帧数。一条 tube 的 T 帧 loss 全部加起来，才除以 tube 数。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`VideoSetCriterion.forward`（与图像版几乎逐字相同）：

```
1. 剔除 aux_outputs，先用主输出做一次匹配
2. num_masks = 批内所有视频的 GT 管道数之和
   → all_reduce 跨卡求和 → 除以 world_size → clamp(min=1)
3. 对 self.losses 中的每项（labels、masks）计算损失
4. 若有 aux_outputs：逐层重新匹配、重新算损失，键名加 "_i" 后缀
5. 返回未加权的损失 dict（乘权重由 VideoMaskFormer.forward 完成）
```

`loss_masks` 的数据流：

```
pred_masks (B, Q, T, H/4, W/4)          GT masks (M, T, H_pad, W_pad)
        │ 按匹配索引选取                       │ 按匹配索引选取、跨视频 cat
        ▼                                     ▼
  (N, T, H/4, W/4) ── flatten(0,1) ──► (N·T, 1, H/4, W/4)
  (N, T, H_pad, W_pad) ─ flatten(0,1) ─► (N·T, 1, H_pad, W_pad)
        │                                     │
        └──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                       ▼
   不确定性引导采样 K=12544 个归一化坐标点
   point_sample 分别在两个分辨率上插值取值
                       ▼
              point_logits/point_labels: (N·T, K)
                       ▼
     loss_mask = BCE(point_logits, point_labels).mean(1).sum() / N
     loss_dice = dice(point_logits, point_labels).sum() / N
```

逐点 BCE 的数学形式（N 为批内管道总数，K 为采样点数）：

\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{mask}} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathrm{BCE}\big(p_{n,t}(x_k),\, g_{n,t}(x_k)\big)
\]

注意分母是 \(N\)（管道数）而不是 \(N \cdot T\)（帧数）。这个选择的含义：

- **一条 tube = 一个样本**：不管视频采了 2 帧还是 36 帧，一个实例对总损失的贡献量级相当（帧数越多单帧权重自然被摊薄，但整条 tube 的贡献不变量级）。
- **与匹配语义对齐**：匹配是把一条 tube 分给一个 query（见 4.2），监督时也把这条 tube 当作一个整体计数单位，两者口径一致。
- **分布式正确性**：与图像版相同，`num_masks` 先 all_reduce 再除以 world_size，保证多卡各自算的 loss 加起来等于「全局批」的损失。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**损失入口与拆帧**。[criterion.py:140-155](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L140-L155)：按匹配索引选出被匹配的预测 mask 与 GT mask，然后 `flatten(0, 1)` 把 (N, T, H, W) 拆成 (N·T, H, W)、`[:, None]` 补上通道维变成 (N·T, 1, H, W)——注释明确写着 `# NT x 1 x H x W`。

```python
src_masks = src_masks[src_idx]
# Modified to handle video
target_masks = torch.cat([t['masks'][i] for t, (_, i) in zip(targets, indices)]).to(src_masks)

# No need to upsample predictions as we are using normalized coordinates :)
# NT x 1 x H x W
src_masks = src_masks.flatten(0, 1)[:, None]
target_masks = target_masks.flatten(0, 1)[:, None]
```

`# Modified to handle video` 这一行注释就是视频版相对图像版的全部改动痕迹之一：GT 用 `torch.cat` 直接拼接。对比图像版 [criterion.py:150-159](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/criterion.py#L150-L159)：图像版必须用 `nested_tensor_from_tensor_list` 把批内不同尺寸的 GT mask pad 成嵌套张量（还留了一个 `TODO use valid to mask invalid areas`），且只做 `[:, None]` 没有 `flatten(0, 1)`——因为图像版没有时间维。

**逐点采样被完整保留**。[criterion.py:157-177](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L157-L177)：在 `torch.no_grad()` 下用 `get_uncertain_point_coords_with_randomness`（3K 候选中按不确定度 \(-|\text{logit}|\) 取 top-0.75K、随机补齐共 12544 点，见 u5-l2）对 N·T 个帧 mask 各自独立采样；`point_sample` 用归一化坐标分别在预测（1/4 分辨率）与 GT（全尺寸）上双线性插值，天然对齐、无需上采样。

**损失与归一化**。[criterion.py:179-186](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L179-L186)：`sigmoid_ce_loss_jit` 内部是 `loss.mean(1).sum() / num_masks`——先对每个帧 mask 的 K 个点取均值，再把 N·T 个帧级损失**求和**，除以管道数 `num_masks`。这就是 4.1.2 公式的代码形态。

**num_masks 数的是管道**。[criterion.py:219-227](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L219-L227)：`num_masks = sum(len(t["labels"]) for t in targets)`。每个 target dict 的 `labels` 长度是该视频的 GT 管道数（`prepare_targets` 中 `valid_idx` 过滤后保留的实例行数），随后 all_reduce、除以 world_size、clamp(min=1)，与图像版逻辑一致但计数单位换成了管道。

**深监督逐层重匹配**。[criterion.py:234-241](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L234-L241)：对每组 `aux_outputs` 重新调用 matcher 再算损失，键名加 `_i` 后缀——与图像版（u5-l3）完全同构。YTVIS 配置 `DEC_LAYERS: 10`，因此损失 dict 共 3 × 10 = 30 个键。

**分类损失与 no-object 降权**。[criterion.py:113-115](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L113-L115) 构造 `empty_weight`（最后一维 no-object 置 `eos_coef=0.1`），[criterion.py:122-138](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/criterion.py#L122-L138) 的 `loss_labels` 用它做加权交叉熵——与图像版逐字相同，不再展开。

**criterion 在哪里被构建与加权**。[video_maskformer_model.py:104-132](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/video_maskformer_model.py#L104-L132)：`from_config` 用 YTVIS 配置的权重（`CLASS_WEIGHT: 2.0`、`MASK_WEIGHT: 5.0`、`DICE_WEIGHT: 5.0`）同时构建 matcher 代价与 `weight_dict`，并把 `weight_dict` 按 `DEC_LAYERS - 1` 展开成带 `_i` 后缀的 30 键（与图像版 u5-l3 同构）；[video_maskformer_model.py:190-203](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/video_maskformer_model.py#L190-L203)：训练分支对 criterion 返回的损失按键加权、丢弃白名单外的键。

**GT masks 从哪来**。[video_maskformer_model.py:227-253](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/video_maskformer_model.py#L227-L253)：`prepare_targets` 为每个视频分配 `[_num_instance, num_frames, h_pad, w_pad]` 的全零 bool 张量（L232），逐帧把 `gt_masks.tensor` 写入左上角（L241），再按 `valid_idx`（`gt_ids != -1` 至少一帧有效，L244）过滤并转 float（L250）。这一步解释了 4.1.1 的第二处差异：**GT 已 pad 到网络输入尺寸且长度统一**，criterion 里才能直接 `torch.cat`。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用随机输入跑一次 `VideoSetCriterion` 前向，确认损失键的构成（主输出 3 键 + 每层 aux 3 键），并手工验证 `num_masks` 的管道计数语义。

**操作步骤**（示例代码，保存为仓库外任意脚本，如 `/tmp/run_video_criterion.py`）：

```python
# 示例代码：随机输入跑 VideoSetCriterion
import torch
from mask2former_video.modeling.criterion import VideoSetCriterion

### 4.2 VideoHungarianMatcher：一次 LSAP 匹配整条时空管道

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`VideoHungarianMatcher` 与图像版 `HungarianMatcher` 逐行对比后会发现：**代价函数、随机采样、fp32 防抖、LSAP 求解全部相同**，唯一的实质差异是 mask 代价的计算维度——图像版把 mask 升成 (Q, 1, H, W) 后采样得到 (Q, K)；视频版把 4D 的 (Q, T, H, W) **直接**交给 `point_sample`，T 被当作「通道维」，采样输出 flatten 后是 (Q, K·T)。

为什么必须**按视频整体**做一次匹配，而不是逐帧独立匹配？因为 query 跨帧共享（u9-l2）：一个 query 对一条 tube 的全部 T 帧负责。若逐帧匹配，同一 GT 实例可能在第 1 帧分给 query A、第 2 帧分给 query B，监督信号自相矛盾，模型永远学不出稳定的「一个 query 一条管道」。把整条 tube 的 T 帧代价压缩进代价矩阵的一个元素，LSAP 一旦把 query A 与 GT 管道 g 绑定，A 就要在**所有帧**上同时逼近 g——跨帧身份一致性由此从监督机制层面得到保障。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

对 batch 中每个视频 b：

```
1. 分类代价：out_prob = pred_logits[b].softmax(-1)          → (Q, K+1)
   cost_class = -out_prob[:, tgt_ids]                        → (Q, M)
2. mask 代价：
   out_mask = pred_masks[b]            # (Q, T, H/4, W/4)  不加通道维！
   tgt_mask = targets[b]["masks"]      # (M, T, H_pad, W_pad) 已 pad
   point_coords = torch.rand(1, K, 2)  # 一组共享的随机归一化坐标
   tgt = point_sample(tgt_mask, coords.repeat(M,1,1)).flatten(1)  # (M, K·T)
   out = point_sample(out_mask, coords.repeat(Q,1,1)).flatten(1)  # (Q, K·T)
   关 autocast 转 fp32：
   cost_mask = batch_sigmoid_ce_loss(out, tgt)   # (Q, M)
   cost_dice = batch_dice_loss(out, tgt)         # (Q, M)
3. C = 2.0·cost_class + 5.0·cost_mask + 5.0·cost_dice   # (Q, M)
4. linear_sum_assignment(C.cpu()) → 一对一匹配对
```

`batch_sigmoid_ce_loss` 中的归一化因子 `hw = inputs.shape[1]` 在视频下变成 \(K \cdot T\)——即每个代价元素是「整条 tube 的所有帧 × 所有点」的平均 BCE，一条 query 与一条 GT 的相似度由全部 T 帧联合决定：

\[
C_{\text{mask}}(q, m) = \frac{1}{K T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathrm{BCE}\big(p_q(x_k, t),\, g_m(x_k, t)\big)
\]

两个值得注意的细节：

- **matcher 用纯随机采样，loss 用不确定性引导采样**。matcher 的 `torch.rand`（L120）与图像版一致；`get_uncertain_point_coords_with_randomness` 只出现在 criterion 侧。匹配发生在梯度更新之前，随机采样足够稳定且更便宜。
- **分辨率不一致无碍**。预测是 1/4 分辨率、GT 是网络输入全尺寸，`point_sample` 的坐标是归一化的 \([0,1]\)，各自乘以各自的空间尺寸后插值，天然对齐——这就是源码注释 `# No need to upsample predictions as we are using normalized coordinates :)` 的含义。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**分类代价**。[matcher.py:105-111](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L105-L111)：softmax 后取负的目标类概率近似 NLL，与图像版逐字相同。

**4D mask 直接进 point_sample**。[matcher.py:113-120](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L113-L120)：`out_mask` 形状为 `[num_queries, T, H_pred, W_pred]`，GT `.to(out_mask)` 只转 dtype/device；图像版的 `out_mask[:, None]` 两行被**注释保留**（L117-118），采样点是 `torch.rand(1, num_points, 2)`——所有 query 与 GT 共享同一组坐标，保证代价在相同像素位置间比较。

**采样与展平**。[matcher.py:122-132](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L122-L132)：`point_sample` 按 (N, P, 2) 坐标对 (N, C, H, W) 输入采样，输出 (N, P, C)。这里输入的「通道维 C」就是 T，输出 (Q, K, T) 经 `flatten(1)` 变 (Q, K·T)。对比图像版 [matcher.py:117-126](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former/modeling/matcher.py#L117-L126)：图像版先 `out_mask[:, None]` 升成 (Q, 1, H, W)，输出 (Q, K) 后 `squeeze(1)`，最终是 (Q, K) 的二维代价输入。

**fp32 防抖与 LSAP**。[matcher.py:134-151](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/modeling/matcher.py#L134-L151)：`autocast(enabled=False)` 内转 float32 计算 BCE/Dice 代价（半精度下逐点插值误差会造成匹配抖动，u5-l1 讲过同一动机）；三项代价按 2.0/5.0/5.0 加权合成 (Q, M) 矩阵，`linear_sum_assignment` 求解一对一分配。整个函数被 `@torch.no_grad()` 包裹（L95），不建计算图。

**谁消费匹配结果**：`VideoSetCriterion.forward` 对主输出与每组 aux 各调一次（criterion.py L218、L237），每次都是「整条 tube」级别的重新匹配。

### 4.3 YTVISEvaluator：从 pred_masks 到 YTVIS AP

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`YTVISEvaluator` 是从 IFC 项目移植的 `DatasetEvaluator`，底层依赖仓库自带的 `YTVOS` / `YTVOSeval` api（cocotools 的视频版变体）。它解决的问题是：模型输出的是「每视频 top-10 个 (score, label, T 帧 mask)」，评估器要把它转成 YTVIS json、与 GT 做**tube 级**匹配，输出 AP 系列指标。

评估与训练监督是两个独立环节，口径有一处重要差别值得点明：训练的匈牙利匹配在「采样点」上比较 mask（省显存），评估的 IoU 在**全部帧的全部像素**上比较（要权威）。

YTVIS 格式的预测条目：

```json
{
  "video_id": 1,
  "score": 0.92,
  "category_id": 3,
  "segmentations": [RLE_t0, RLE_t1, null, RLE_t3, ...]   // 每帧一个 RLE，缺失帧为 null
}
```

GT 标注同构（多了 `areas`、`iscrowd` 等字段），一条 GT 标注就是一条贯穿全视频的实例轨道（u9-l3）。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

评估器生命周期（`reset → process × N → evaluate`）与三段式计算：

```
process（每视频一次）
  inputs（单视频 dict，含 video_id/length）+ outputs（inference_video 的 dict）
    → instances_to_coco_json_video
    → [{video_id, score, category_id, segmentations: [T 个 RLE]}, ...]

evaluate（数据集跑完一次）
  gather 到主进程 → 落盘 instances_predictions.pth
  → _eval_predictions
      ① category_id 反映射：模型连续 id → 数据集原始 id
      ② 落盘 results.json
      ③ _evaluate_predictions_on_coco：
           删除 bbox 字段（面积按 mask 算）
           YTVOS api loadRes（计算 avg_area）
           YTVOSeval(gt, dt)：maxDets=[1,10,100]
           evaluate() → accumulate() → summarize()
      ④ _derive_coco_results：从 stats 取 8 项指标 ×100 + per-category AP
```

**时空 IoU** 是整个评估的基石，YTVOSeval 对每对（预测 tube, GT tube）计算：

\[
\text{IoU}_{\text{tube}}(p, g) = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}|p_t \cap g_t|}{\displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}|p_t \cup g_t|}
\]

逐帧累加交集与并集的像素数再相除。三种帧状态的处理：

| 该帧预测 | 该帧 GT | 交集 | 并集 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 有 | 有 | \(|p_t \cap g_t|\) | \(|p_t \cup g_t|\) |
| 无（null） | 有 | 0 | \(|g_t|\)（漏检帧全额惩罚） |
| 有 | 无（GT 缺失帧） | 0 | \(|p_t|\)（虚检惩罚） |

这个定义意味着：预测只要**漏掉一帧**，该帧整个 GT 面积就进入分母——tube IoU 断崖式下跌。这是 VIS 远难于图像实例分割、AP 数值普遍偏低的算法根源，也是「跨帧身份一致性」被直接量化的方式：一个 query 若中途「换目标」，整条 tube 同时变成一条 FP（对真目标）和一条 FN。

**面积分桶口径**：APs/APm/APl 按 `avg_area`（tube 的**逐帧平均面积**，而非全帧总面积）划分，阈值 128²/256²。长视频里的小物体不会因为帧数多、总面积大而被错划为 large。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**process 的输入契约与图像版完全不同**。[ytvis_eval.py:103-113](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/data_video/ytvis_eval.py#L103-L113)：断言 `len(inputs) == 1`（视频测试加载器恒 batch=1，u9-l3），`outputs` 是 dict 而非图像版的 `Instances` 列表。dict 的三个键正是 `inference_video` 的输出（[video_maskformer_model.py:280-285](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/9b0651c6c1d5b3af2e6da0589b719c514ec0d69a/mask2former_video/video_maskformer_model.py#L280-L285)）：`pred_scores` / `pred_labels` / `pred_masks`（每个元素是 (T, H, W) 的 bool 张量）。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `VideoSetCriterion.loss_masks` **完整保留**了图像版的逐点采样损失（不确定性引导 + `point_sample`），真实差异只有两处：GT 因 `prepare_targets` 已 pad 而直接 `torch.cat`，以及 `flatten(0, 1)` 把 (N, T, H, W) 的 tube 拆成 (N·T, 1, H, W) 的帧 mask 逐帧监督。
- 归一化分母 `num_masks` 数的是**管道数**而非帧数：一条 tube 的 T 帧 loss 求和后除以 tube 数，「一条 tube = 一个样本」，与匹配语义严格对齐，且跨卡 all_reduce 平均保证分布式正确。
- `VideoHungarianMatcher` 与图像版唯一的实质差异是 mask 代价的维度：4D 的 (Q, T, H, W) 直接交给 `point_sample`（T 充当通道维），`flatten(1)` 后每个代价元素是 K·T 个采样点的联合损失——一次 LSAP 把整条 tube 绑定给一个 query，跨帧身份一致性从监督机制上得到保障。
- `YTVISEvaluator` 基于 IFC 移植的 `YTVOS`/`YTVOSeval` api：预测逐帧 RLE 编码成 `segmentations` 列表，时空 IoU 按「逐帧交集像素和 ÷ 逐帧并集像素和」计算，漏帧全额惩罚；指标取 stats 前 8 项（AP/AP50/AP75/APs/APm/APl/AR1/AR10），面积分桶按 `avg_area`（逐帧平均面积）。
- `--eval-only` 路径：`main → Trainer.test → inference_on_dataset(autocast) → YTVISEvaluator.evaluate`，结果见于两份文件（`inference/results.json`、`inference/instances_predictions.pth`）与三处日志（12 行标准表、segm 小表 + 分类表、csv 打印）；视频无 TTA（`NotImplementedError`）。
- 训练与评估对「mask 相似度」的口径不同：匹配在采样点上比（省显存），评估在全部像素上比（要权威），但两者都以 tube 为原子单位。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. - Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
